trust_decision.summary: Whether internal detail (the inspected non-%Plug.Conn{} handler return) may be sent to the client is decided by typed_controller_show_raised_errors?; the rescue path consults it, but unexpected_return builds the 500 message from inspect(value) unconditionally.

landing_point.why: The summary names the route handler return value echoed into the error response; unexpected_return is the only place that builds 'Route handler must return %Plug.Conn{}, got: ...' and sits beside the already-gated rescue.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP: any typed_controller route action generated by GenerateController (lib/ash_typescript/typed_controller/transformers/generate_controller.ex:24-25) whose fn/2 run handler returns a non-conn (dispatch at request_handler.ex:227-232)
HTTP: same generated route action, module-based Route handler (handler.run/2) returning a non-conn; same unexpected_return sink

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Only source change besides request_handler.ex is a docstring in lib/ash_typescript.ex:640-645 (fix.diff:328-335)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None that holds: the only sink is unexpected_return, next to the already-gated rescue clause; the guide even documents the leaky message as intended output (documentation/guides/typed-controllers.md:357-373), which a solver might use to argue to keep it, but the advisory states the opposite.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: 422 validation errors must keep their detailed messages (cast/constraint messages incl. Exception.message of cast errors), and show_raised_errors=true must still return the inspected value; the fix test also asserts the detail is logged server-side. An over-broad fix that genericises every error from send_errors breaks these.

module Route handler (run/2) returning a non-conn term

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already present as legitimate validation output; a planted variant that inspects the raw cast error term (not just its message) is a plausible maintainer shortcut, but it is a where-type sibling in the same file.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The RPC side needed an explicit fail-closed fix, so a typed-controller copy that falls back to the raw error on handler crash would be a believable oversight.
